solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Was in right place to take ages with journalist

blocks.note: to take ages is to be long, read as one run of letters
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: Someone who arrived on time keeps company with a slow-moving reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'to take ages' has to be turned into 'to be long' before it yields letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong somewhere is to be in your proper place, so the past tense matches 'was in right place'.

clue.text: Plug at first fits badly

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word that follows it

blocks.note: the opening letter of fits
ill can mean badly, as in ill-judged

explanation.surface: A stopper that doesn't sit snugly in the hole it was meant for.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a gap and to fill it are synonyms as verbs, both meaning to stop up a hole.

clue.text: Seat is awkward for nap

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsily arranged, so these letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An uncomfortable chair makes it hard to doze off.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a short afternoon sleep, a synonym for a nap, borrowed from Spanish.

clue.text: Temperature lowered, subjected to banter

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
to ease something down is to lower it

explanation.surface: A fever comes down and the patient gets ribbed about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teased has been mocked playfully, which is being on the receiving end of banter.

clue.text: Retire an unreliable old servant

indicators.note: unreliable suggests letters that cannot be trusted to stay in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pensioning off a household helper who can no longer be depended on.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a servant kept on long in a household, often an elderly family servant.

clue.text: Tree, mark, is solidly rooted

blocks.note: a fir is a kind of tree
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A tree with a blaze on its trunk stands deeply anchored in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means fixed and stable, which is how something solidly rooted stays in place.

clue.text: Certain to explain about the computer industry

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to define a term is to explain it
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: Someone is sure they can describe what goes on in the tech business.
explanation.definitionFit: Definite and certain are synonyms, both meaning settled beyond doubt.

clue.text: Magnificent online film

blocks.note: E, as in e-mail, stands for electronic or online
pic is informal for a picture or movie

explanation.surface: A rave review of a movie being streamed on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is used informally to mean impressive or grand on a heroic scale.

clue.text: Lots of dogs off the lead

indicators.note: off the lead says the leading letter is set loose and dropped

blocks.note: poodles are a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Plenty of dogs running free in the park without leashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the lead' is the dog-walker's phrase for unleashed; here it removes the lead letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, just like lots.

clue.text: Small appreciative crowd

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a warm reception is an appreciative one

explanation.surface: A modest audience that nevertheless applauds enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' and 'appreciative' look like adjectives on the crowd, but each supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large dense mass of people or insects, so it serves as a synonym for crowd.

clue.text: So embarrassed, if this is curling

definitions.text: So embarrassed, if this is curling

blocks.note: surface reading: someone squirming with shame
setter's reading: the body part whose curling names a cringeworthy feeling

explanation.walkthrough: Something toe-curling is so embarrassing it makes you squirm; the clue asks which part of the foot does the curling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom toe-curling describes acute embarrassment, so the digit that curls is the answer.

clue.text: Half of us heard goose in the country

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word leaves just one of its letters, here the front one
heard means we want what the ear catches, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: the first half of us
a gander is a male goose; in a non-rhotic accent it ends like the -da here

explanation.surface: Part of a group listens to a goose somewhere out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like rural land but means a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a country in East Africa, so it is an example of a nation.

clue.text: Weapon I stuck into head — pilot must report this

indicators.note: stuck into means pushed inside another word, which then surrounds it

blocks.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
taken as written
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness

explanation.surface: An aviator files a report after a weapon was jammed into someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland or promontory, common in British place names such as Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss between aircraft is a dangerous incident pilots are required to file a report about.

clue.text: Very enthusiastic type drawing plenty back into party

indicators.note: back says the word is read from its end to its start
drawing means pulling something in, so one word is pulled inside another
into names the word that receives the pulled-in piece and surrounds it

blocks.note: many means plenty
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: An eager guest pulls lots of people back to the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' looks like sketching but means pulling in.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo, literally a generator, is figuratively a person full of energy and drive.

clue.text: "Motorway pace" — should have read "Motorway race"?

blocks.note: surface reading: a phrase about driving speed
setter's reading: one wrong letter on the page, a typesetting slip

explanation.walkthrough: The clue shows the error it names: P stands where R was meant, the kind of slip a proofreader catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongly printed character in a text is called a typographical error of this sort.

clue.text: I had cared to relinquish European personal document?

indicators.note: to relinquish is to give up, so a letter is let go from the word

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone once concerned about giving up their EU paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'personal document' is a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity card is a document carried by a person to prove who they are.

clue.text: Rush round part of UK for something to go with coffee

indicators.note: round means placed around, so one word encircles the other

blocks.note: to dash is to rush
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A hurried trip around a region of Britain in search of a coffee accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish is a sweet pastry, commonly eaten alongside a cup of coffee.

clue.text: Trees in front, stone behind

blocks.note: fore means at the front
ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A garden layout: woodland in the foreground and a rock behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' just places the stone piece after the front piece. A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area covered with trees, so trees collectively stand for it.

clue.text: Female stiff and unresponsive

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
rigid means stiff

explanation.surface: A description of a woman as cold and starchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid literally means very cold and figuratively describes someone emotionally cold and unresponsive.

clue.text: Song is broadcast

blocks.note: first meaning: a tune or melody
second meaning: to transmit on radio or television

explanation.surface: A track gets played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple melody, and to air a programme is to transmit it.

clue.text: Be very busy with a new person

blocks.note: a place that hums is bustling with activity
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Being swamped with work because of a fresh recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A human is a person, a member of humankind.

clue.text: Enormously fat, good to be in the shade

indicators.note: to be in says one letter sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a hue is a shade of colour
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A large person happily sitting out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' suggests shelter from the sun, but here it is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge means extremely large, so describing someone as enormously fat fits it.

clue.text: Worker perhaps abandons vital foreign consignment

indicators.note: abandons says one piece leaves the longer word

blocks.note: vital means important
an ant is an example of a worker; perhaps marks the example

explanation.surface: An employee walks away from an essential shipment from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'worker' is very often an ant or bee.
explanation.definitionFit: An import is goods brought in from abroad, a consignment from a foreign country.

clue.text: Dog conceals large part of tooth

indicators.note: conceals means the first word hides another inside itself

blocks.note: a pup is a young dog
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A dog hides a big chunk of a tooth it has chewed off.
explanation.definitionFit: The pulp is the soft inner tissue of a tooth containing nerves and blood vessels.

clue.text: Food, wise to distribute between baskets, they say

definitions.text: wise to distribute between baskets, they say

blocks.note: first meaning: something eaten, especially at breakfast

blocks.clueFragment: wise to distribute between baskets, they say
blocks.note: second meaning: what the proverb warns against putting all in one basket

explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' points to a proverb, not a sound-alike: don't put all your eggs in one basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are a common food, and the well-known proverb names them as the things to spread across several baskets.

clue.text: Son prepared to be drinking greedily

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
willing means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: A boy who is ready to be guzzling.
explanation.definitionFit: Swilling means gulping drink in large quantities, a synonym for drinking greedily.
